case.description: A correct answer. Full marks; the limits check should confirm 2 V at t = 0 and 5 V at infinity.
case.solution: (a) tau = RC = 10e3 * 100e-6 = 1 s. (b) The capacitor voltage cannot jump, so v_C(0+) = 2 V, and the final value is 5 V. v_C(t) = 5 - 3 e^{-t} V for t >= 0.

case.description: The classic mistake: v_C(t) = 5(1 - e^{-t}), as if the capacitor started empty. Only the initial-value item is lost; the limits check should point out that the expression gives 0 V at t = 0, not 2 V.
case.solution: (a) tau = RC = 1 s. (b) The capacitor charges toward 5 V: v_C(t) = 5(1 - e^{-t}) V.

case.description: Right limits, wrong exponent: e^{-t RC} with tau written in units of seconds squared. The exponential item is lost; the units check should say the exponent is not dimensionless.
case.solution: (a) tau = RC = 1 s^2. (b) v_C(t) = 5 - 3 e^{-t RC} V.
